The OTP is stuck at the door. Let’s put it in the app

Today the delivery OTP reaches shoppers only once the partner is already at the door. Miss that window and the parcel goes back. This pre-read shows the problem first, then a proposal.

01 — How handover works today

The OTP is created at the door, and only works at the door

Every delivery depends on a few minutes in which the shopper must get, read and pass on a 4-digit code.

01

Partner reaches the door

The parcel is already outside the house.

02

Partner triggers the OTP

The code is created only now.

03

OTP lands on WhatsApp

Sometimes at out-for-delivery, always at the door.

04

Shopper reads it out

Only if they have their phone, signal and a free moment.

05

Parcel handed over

Miss the window and the visit is wasted.

Delivery day
Door

Orange = the only minutes in which the OTP can do its job today.

02 — What shoppers see today

Nowhere in the app shows the OTP today

Current post-order screens from the Design SoT (Pre-Delivery).

03 — Where it breaks

Shoppers aren’t ignoring the OTP. They can’t get to it in time

Low network

The OTP message doesn’t arrive while the partner is waiting.

Dead battery or no SIM

The phone that should get the OTP can’t be reached at all.

In a meeting or at work

The shopper can’t pick up the call or read the message in time.

Someone else is at home

Family can take the parcel, but the code is on a phone that isn’t there.

Reasons from the self-pickup research. The fourth card follows from them: the parcel can be received by anyone, the OTP can’t.

04 — One parcel, three visits

How a missed OTP turns into a returned order

Day 1 · 10:40

The parcel arrives while Priya is at her office

Her sister is home and ready to take it. The OTP lands on Priya’s phone, 14 km away. By the time she reads it, the partner has left.

Attempt 1 failed
Day 2 · 12:15

She’s in a meeting when the partner calls

The call and the OTP come in together. She sees both an hour later.

Attempt 2 failed
Day 3 · 11:05

The office basement has no signal

The OTP never arrives. The partner marks the order undeliverable after his attempts run out.

Return to origin
Day 4

Priya gets a refund instead of her shoes

The parcel goes back to origin. After three wasted days, she decides her next order goes to Flipkart.

Next order on Flipkart

Illustrative story built from the reasons shoppers gave in research, not a single participant’s account.

05 — Evidence

Some shoppers already chose self-pickup to avoid this

In the self-pickup research, part of the reason shoppers adopted self-pickup was the OTP: the parcel is handed to the shopkeeper, and the shopper gives the OTP only when they go to collect it.

Shoppers

Delays and drop-off

Return to origin

08 — User stories

What each side needs from the handover

As a shopper at work, I want to share the delivery OTP with my family before the partner arrives, so that the parcel is received on the first visit.

As a family member at home, I want to see the OTP the shopper sent me, so that I can receive the parcel without calling them.

As a shopper with patchy network, I want to find the OTP in the app instead of waiting for a message, so that a weak signal doesn’t cost me the delivery.

As a delivery partner, I want to get the OTP on my first visit, so that I don’t lose time and earnings on repeat trips.

As a Meesho post-order team, I want to cut failed attempts caused by OTP handover, so that fewer orders go back to origin.

09 — Outside-in

Flipkart already puts the OTP on the order page

Flipkart’s Order Details shows the delivery OTP in-app, under “Keep in mind at doorstep”.

It pairs the OTP with a doorstep reminder, “Verify item before sharing OTP”, so the code arrives with an instruction rather than as a bare SMS.

For a shopper like Priya, that’s the app she’d move her next order to.

Now, the proposal
10 — Proposal

Show the OTP all day, wherever the shopper looks first

On delivery day the OTP sits in the app, ready to copy or forward on WhatsApp to whoever is at home. The WhatsApp message keeps going out as it does today.

Prototype walkthrough

The OTP stays in view, from Home to Order details

  1. Home shows the OTP strip above the nav. As the shopper scrolls the feed, it drops down, shrinks and fades out.
  2. My Orders tab: the out-for-delivery card carries the OTP chip.
  3. Tap the card to open the order.
  4. Order details opens with the Delivery OTP card in view, ready to copy or share.

Animated walkthrough of the Figma screens, ease-in-out transitions, loops every 14 s.

11 — Decisions to make

Three calls the design leaves open

A · Show the OTP from out-for-delivery

option

OTP is generated when the order goes out for delivery and stays visible all day. Simplest change to today’s OTP logic; the shopper gets a few hours to share it.

B · Generate at shipping, show on delivery day

option

OTP is created at shipping and unlocks on delivery day. The shopper can plan the handover the night before, but OTP generation moves earlier in the logistics flow.

C · Home strip

needs exception

A floating strip over the Home feed sits on the high rung of the homepage attention ladder, so it needs a GM + CPO exception. Fallback: an inline banner on Home, or Order details + My Orders only.
